turns.doctor_question: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um, well, I'm hoping I'm in the right place. It's probably nothing too serious, but... well, I guess what brings me in is that whenever I'm supposed to just sit quietly—like in our staff meetings at work, or, you know, church event briefings—I get this feeling. 

It’s sort of like... like I've got a motor humming under my skin. I always try really hard to be respectful and pay attention, I really do, but I just end up shifting around in my chair a lot, or I'll stand up in the back, or find some polite excuse to move around a bit. 

Is... is that the kind of thing you need to know? I hope I'm explaining it okay.

symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient describes shifting around in their chair a lot when expected to sit quietly.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient states they stand up or find excuses to move around during meetings where they are supposed to remain seated.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes a subjective feeling of restlessness, comparing it to having a 'motor humming under my skin'.

turns.doctor_question: Have you had this difficulty sitting still since you were a child?
turns.patient_response:
Well, um... yes, I suppose I have. I mean, I was always just a very, you know, energetic boy, but... I do remember getting into a little bit of trouble back in grade school for it. Nothing too terrible, I promise! Just... I had a habit of popping out of my seat when I wasn't supposed to. 

And sometimes I'd accidentally talk over the teacher, or I'd rush ahead and start doing things before the directions were even finished. I never meant to be disrespectful, I really didn't, I just got so eager to get going, you know? My mother... well, she used to say I acted like I was wound a little too tight, even as a kid. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.

symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient explicitly recalls a habit of 'popping out of my seat when I wasn't supposed to' during grade school.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient describes being a very energetic boy who was 'eager to get going' and whose mother said he acted like he was 'wound a little too tight'.
symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient admits to accidentally talking over the teacher, indicating interrupting others.
